# synology_network (Resource)

DSM hostname, DNS and general network policy. Interface addresses, DHCP leases and default routes have separate owners. A change can interrupt DSM connectivity; retain an independent management path and apply separately from router changes. Destroy leaves network settings unchanged.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "synology_network" "nas" {
  hostname   = "nas"
  manual_dns = false
  ipv4_first = true
}
import {
  to = synology_network.nas
  id = "network"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `arp_ignore` (Boolean) Use DSM ARP reply isolation.
- `hostname` (String) NAS NetBIOS hostname. Changing it can affect discovery and certificate names.
- `ip_conflict_detection` (Boolean) Enable IP address conflict detection.
- `ipv4_first` (Boolean) Prefer IPv4 when resolving remote hosts.
- `manual_dns` (Boolean) Use explicitly configured DNS servers rather than DHCP DNS.
- `multiple_gateways` (Boolean) Enable multiple gateways. Routes and interface addresses are not configured here.
- `primary_dns` (String) Primary DNS address. Omission retains the freshly observed value.
- `secondary_dns` (String) Secondary DNS address, or an empty string.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Singleton identity and import identifier: network. Destroy only releases Terraform management; it never resets DSM settings.
